title: Roman Twelve Tables Prohibit Malevolent Spells
description: The Roman Twelve Tables (c. 450 BCE) include provisions against malevolent magic, specifically prohibiting the use of incantations (defixiones) to harm neighbors' crops and cattle. This represents one of the earliest codifications of magic as a legal offense in Western history. The law distinguishes between harmful magic directed against persons and property, establishing a pattern of legal engagement with magical practice that will persist through Roman legal tradition. Scholars such as Richard Gordon and Fritz Graf have analyzed these provisions as evidence of widespread anxiety about magical harm in Roman society.
historiographical_note: Fritz Graf and Richard Gordon have examined these provisions as foundational to the Roman legal tradition on magic, noting the distinction between harmful and protective magic already implicit in early Roman law.
source_method: Published scholarship; primary legal sources (Pliny NH 28.17-18; Gaius Institutes)
